title: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) Retinopathy: The Definitive Screening Guide
summary: A comprehensive clinical roadmap for the prevention, screening, and management of Plaquenil-induced maculopathy based on the 2016 AAO Guidelines. Essential for ophthalmologists managing patients with RA and SLE.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), commercially known as Plaquenil, is a 4-aminoquinoline derivative used for Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). While safer than chloroquine, it carries a risk of irreversible, vision-threatening toxic maculopathy. The primary mechanism involves binding to melanin in the Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE), leading to metabolic disruption and subsequent loss of photoreceptors.

rows: The most important predictor; exceeds metabolic clearance.
Cumulative dose increases risk; risk is <1% before 5 years.
HCQ is cleared renally; reduced GFR doubles toxicity risk.
Synergistic toxicity; 5x increased risk of retinopathy.
Masks early toxicity signs and interferes with screening.

sections.title: The AAO Screening Schedule
content: Step 1: Baseline Exam (Within 1st year of starting HCQ) to rule out pre-existing maculopathy.
Step 2: Annual Screening begins after 5 years of treatment for low-risk patients.
Step 3: Immediate Annual Screening if 'High Risk' factors (e.g., Tamoxifen, Renal failure) are present.
Step 4: Frequent Monitoring if 'Borderline' findings are detected on OCT or VF.

content.explanation: D: Dose (>5mg/kg), D: Duration (>5yrs), R: Renal (Low GFR), T: Tamoxifen, M: Macular disease.

branches: SD-OCT: Look for 'Flying Saucer' sign (EZ loss)
mfERG: Objective mapping of paracentral cone function
Wide-field Imaging: Mandatory for Asian patients

sections.title: Subjective Screening: Visual Fields
content: Automated Perimetry is mandatory.
Standard: 10-2 SITA Standard/Fast protocol.
Look for 'Paracentral' or 'Ring' scotomas.
Pattern Deviation plot is more sensitive than Mean Deviation.
Asian Population Requirement: 30-2 or 24-2 (toxicity is often extramacular/peripheral).

sections.title: Pathognomonic OCT Findings
content: Loss of the Ellipsoid Zone (EZ) in the paracentral region.
Thinning of the Outer Nuclear Layer (ONL).
The 'Flying Saucer' Sign: Sparing of the foveal EZ creates a central 'island' appearance.
Late Stage: Total RPE and outer retinal atrophy.

sections.title: The Asian Phenotype Variation
content: Toxicity in Asian patients typically presents OUTSIDE the macula.
10-2 Visual Fields will MISS 50% of toxicity in this population.
Must perform 30-2 Visual Fields and Wide-field OCT/FAF.

sections.title: Ineffective Screening Methods (Do NOT Use)
content: Amsler Grid: Too insensitive for early detection.
Color Vision Testing: Non-specific and late-stage finding.
Fundus Photography: Misses early structural changes.
Full-field ERG: Only abnormal in end-stage disease.

rows: Presents earlier, 'Pisciform' flecks on FAF, dark choroid on FFA.
Progressive decrease in VA, abnormal Full-field ERG early.
Presence of Drusen, Pigmentary changes not confined to ring.
History of sun gazing, small foveal 'hole' on OCT.

sections.title: Management & Cessation Protocol
content: Step 1: Confirm findings with at least two different modalities (e.g., OCT + VF).
Step 2: Documentation: Detail the severity and risk of continued use.
Step 3: Multi-disciplinary Communication: Formally write to the Rheumatologist to advise cessation.
Step 4: Transition: Rheumatologist must switch to an alternative agent (e.g., Methotrexate, biologics).
Step 5: Follow-up: Continue monitoring for 1-2 years after stopping due to 'coasting'.

sections.title: The 'Coasting' Phenomenon
content: Retinopathy can continue to progress for 1-3 years AFTER drug cessation.
This is due to the extremely long half-life of HCQ in pigmented tissues.
Early detection is CRITICAL; if damage is foveal, it will likely worsen despite stopping.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Practice
content: Always use ACTUAL body weight for dosing (not Ideal weight).
Cumulative dose over 1000g is a major threshold for concern.
If the patient is on Tamoxifen, the risk is 'Extreme'.
Bull’s Eye Maculopathy is a LATE sign; the goal is to find sub-clinical change.

sections.title: Recent Landmark Studies
sections.content: The Melles & Marmor (2014) study in JAMA Ophthalmology revolutionized current dosing. It demonstrated that 5mg/kg actual weight was the most predictive safety threshold, significantly reducing the incidence of toxicity compared to previous dosing guidelines.
